chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Ribat and Abdullah ibn Jabalat, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who had children, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. So what should be done with the inheritance of the man for the absent one from his father? He said: 'It is set aside until he comes.' I said: 'So upon his wealth is Zakat?' He said: 'No, until he comes.' I said: 'So if he comes, does he purify it?' He said: 'No, until a year passes with it being in his hand.' So I said: 'The man is lost and does not come?' He said: 'If the inheritors of the man are reliable with his wealth, they distribute it among themselves. So whenever he comes, they return it to him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the inheritance and Zakat of a missing person whose whereabouts are unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential handling of a missing heir (al-gha'ib), establishing that his share is segregated and exempt from Zakat until his return, with distribution to other heirs only if he remains absent. It highlights the Shia principle of preserving the missing person's rights while allowing estate liquidity, reflecting the Imams' practical approach to inheritance disputes. The ruling underscores the balance between finality in estate settlement and the potential for restitution upon the heir's reappearance.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ibn Rabat and Abdullah Bin Jabalat, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the first, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had children for him, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. So what should be done with the inheritance of the man, for the absent one from his father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Keep it aside until he comes’. I said, ‘So upon his wealth is the Zakat?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until he comes’. I said, ‘So if he comes, he has to purify it (by paying Zakat)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until there turns a year with it being in his hands’. So I said, ‘The man is lost and does not come?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the inheritors of the man can be relied upon with his wealth, so distribute it between them. So whenever he comes, it should be returned to him’.
en.sarwar: 8. Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah, from ibn Ribat and ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has several sons, of whom one disappeared and he did not know where he was. The man died. What must be done with his share of legacy from his father? He (the Imam) said, ‘It must be kept aside until he comes? I then asked if there is Zakat on his assets. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, there is no Zakat until he comes? I then asked if he must pay Zakat when he comes. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, until one year passes with the asset in his possession? I then said, ‘The man is lost and he has not come back? He (the Imam) said, ‘If the heirs of the man can be trusted about his assets, they can distribute it among themselves and when he comes give it to him?”
